Glenroyal Hotel And Shoda Café Minstrel Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Audience
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist for David O'Meara and Colin Keane; recent form reads 3-0-0-0-9-2 with just one placed effort from 12 in similar going, and at 38 days since last run needs this style of race to produce a clean late lane that may not materialise in a small, compressed field.|

runners_data.name: Big Gossey
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a W J Lee booking and two recent wins on Good ground over 6f, stepping back up to 7f where his 1-4P record in similar conditions looks excellent; genuine prominent racer who should slot naturally just behind Power Blue and be ideally positioned throughout.|

runners_data.name: East Hampton
runners_data.note: David Marnane's four-year-old has been placed twice in similar going over this trip and Luke McAteer keeps the ride; a natural front-runner-to-prominent type who should secure second or third rank behind Power Blue, though his record shows no win at this level and he has not fired on soft variants of the track.|

runners_data.name: Zodiac Bear
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's four-year-old has two wins and two places in five Good-ground starts and Ben Coen is a high-quality booking; by nature a prominent racer, he will find himself tucked behind the natural leaders here through congestion rather than intent, which represents a slight compromising of his optimal setup — though his class means he remains dangerous if a gap appears.|

runners_data.name: Duckadilly
runners_data.note: The most recent winner in the field (1st, 10 days ago), Duckadilly has a strong record of four wins from eleven Good-ground runs; Scott McCullagh rides a horse who prefers to race prominently, but space at the head of the pack will be tight and he will be racing fractionally out of character, which tempers confidence despite his sharp recent form.|

runners_data.name: Dorset
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old won twice on soft ground last season but has returned figures of 7-8-9 in 2025 on Good, suggesting the current underfoot conditions may not be bringing out his best; Ryan Moore will attempt to recover position from further back than ideal, and the pattern of big trainers' horses in this scenario suggests he needs a marked return to form.|

runners_data.name: Power Blue
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's three-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner and Rossa Ryan has the licence to bowl clear in a seven-runner field; his recent form has been consistently midfield on Good ground over further, and while the solo lead is a tactical asset, the STYLE_FIT flag signals that sustaining that advantage against classier rivals for the full seven furlongs on fast ground is a genuine question.|

races.paceDynamic: Power Blue is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just seven runners at Curragh's 7f on Good to Firm ground, Rossa Ryan can dictate an honest but controlled tempo without meaningful pressure from a rival pacemaker. Big Gossey and East Hampton are the legitimate prominent horses likely to track Power Blue in second and third, creating a compact, well-strung-out group rather than a scramble for position early. The field contains a glut of natural front-running and prominent types — Zodiac Bear, Dorset, and Duckadilly are all genuine pace-seekers who cannot all secure their preferred slot and will be forced to settle slightly further back than ideal, blunting their tactical options. With a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable Good to Firm tempo and the chasing pack tightly grouped, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-mid racers who can travel close to the pace without burning petrol, then unleash a clean turn of foot in the straight — hold-up horses face a wall if the pace is measured and gaps are scarce late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Power Blue Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Power Blue is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a fair but controlled tempo that suits horses travelling just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Rossa Ryan gets the dream lead in a small field on Good to Firm ground, rationing his effort and quickening from the front inside the final two furlongs; the proximity riders who have settled just behind on a good rhythm are positioned to pounce without having to make up excessive ground. Big Gossey and East Hampton, as the genuine prominent types who slot in second and third, are ideally placed to capitalise if Power Blue's stride shortens close home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses; Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Power Blue goes off at an overly-conservative gallop and the field bunches, creating a sprint finish that drags hold-up horses into contention.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian early tempo compresses the field, negating the advantage of prominent positioning and opening a late lane for Audience to be produced with a powerful late run by Colin Keane; on Good to Firm ground the straight at Curragh is fast enough to reward a horse with a high cruising speed who has been saving energy. Audience's recent form figures are modest but the pace scenario here is the one shape that genuinely suits a hold-up type coming from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrap, Settler Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the displaced prominent types — Zodiac Bear, Dorset, and Duckadilly — contest position early and the race is fractionally hotter in the first three furlongs than Power Blue intends.
scenarios.body: Extra early pressure lifts the tempo just enough to test the front runner's stamina, bringing the race back to a contest of class and finishing kick rather than tactical comfort; horses who were pushed back from their natural slot but can still get a clean run in the straight benefit from the stronger gallop. Zodiac Bear, despite being mapped out of position, has a 2W2P record in similar going and is trained by JP Murtagh who will have him primed to handle an honest pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Break, Field Resets
scenarios.trigger: If there is a slow or ragged start that scrambles early positions and negates Power Blue's ability to establish a clean lead.
scenarios.body: A messy early phase forces jockeys to make ground prematurely and turns the race into a contest of raw ability over the final three furlongs; horses with a high RPR ceiling and good recent form over the trip benefit most when the tactical plan is torn up from the start. Dorset, though out of form lately, carries the Aidan O'Brien stamp and Ryan Moore's tactical nous could see him exploit the confusion better than most.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Zodiac Bear, Dorset, or Duckadilly — all natural prominent types — contest the early positions aggressively, as any scrimmage for the rail in the first furlong could lift the tempo sharply and fundamentally alter the race shape from the controlled scenario Power Blue's team will want.

Monitor Power Blue's margin at the two-furlong pole: if Rossa Ryan has not established a clear solo lead by then, the compressed field behind may produce a wall of horses that leaves no room for late runners like Audience.

Big Gossey's draw and early positioning will be critical — at nine years old and dropping back to 7f, W J Lee needs to slot him smoothly into the perfect tracking position behind the leader from the first furlong or valuable energy will be spent fighting for berth.

The Good to Firm ground (confirmed by the going report for this race) is faster than the card header suggests — horses who have run poorly on soft in recent runs but have strong records on quicker surfaces (notably Zodiac Bear and Duckadilly) may be materially better placed than their recent form implies.

Dorset's last five runs show a steep decline from dual soft-ground winner to three consecutive near-last finishes on Good; if Ryan Moore opts for a positional gamble rather than settling in the rear, it is worth noting whether the horse travels with the same fluency as his two-year-old campaign.

races.name: Racing World 50th Anniversary Irish EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Orchidaceae
runners_data.note: Strong form in similar Good-ground handicaps (winning 7f and 8f on Good), wearing headgear today, and W J Lee is a capable handler of hold-up fillies — the key question is whether a moderate pace off a lone front-runner ever generates enough late sectionals to bring her into contention from the back of six.

runners_data.name: Pink Oxalis
runners_data.note: Blinkered and with decent turf form, but her record of 2W2P from 15 similar-going runs is modest and her last win came on Standard; at 37 days since her last run she is the freshest in the field, though a small-field solo-pace scenario is structurally difficult for a genuine hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Mallavelly
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and partnered by Colin Keane, who will know exactly how to exploit an uncontested lead; she is racing out of her most comfortable stylistic role in the sense that she is usually set an easy task up front, but that is precisely what she gets here — treat the style-fit flag as a competitive note rather than a concern about her position.

runners_data.name: Sanctijude
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good ground and shapes as the natural pressing filly from second or third, with Dylan Browne McMonagle a strong ally in a race where sitting just off the leader is a prime tactical position; her 3-year-old allowance (124lbs) is a genuine asset in this older-horse handicap.

runners_data.name: Kirkland Sioux
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner whose most recent win came over this exact trip on Good ground, but with Mallavelly already taking the lead, Declan McDonogh will likely have to restrain her into midfield — that against-the-grain positioning and the style-fit discount make her a harder horse to rely on here despite her course-trip form.

runners_data.name: Glitter And Glory
runners_data.note: Only 6 days since her last run (which could indicate freshness or fatigue) and another genuine prominent type who wants to be forward but cannot be in this shape; trained by Mrs John Harrington whose yard is 0/24 in the 14-day window, and the style-fit penalty reflects the structural problem of two natural front-runners being redistributed in the same small field.

races.paceDynamic: Mallavelly is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh, and with no genuine pressure expected she should be able to control fractions from the outset and set a sustainable, honest gallop over the mile. Kirkland Sioux and Glitter And Glory are both natural prominent-racing types but, with Mallavelly already occupying the front position, at least one and likely both will be shuffled into a midfield role against their instincts — Colin Keane on Mallavelly is well capable of exploiting any hesitation behind him. The two genuine hold-up fillies, Orchidaceae and Pink Oxalis, will be anchored at the rear and will need the pace to be honest enough to bring them into play turning for home, but with only one horse genuinely setting the fractions that is not guaranteed. This race shape — a lone front-runner on fast ground dictating to a small, compressed field — strongly favours those who can race prominently or press from second, and particularly the front-runner herself if she meets little challenge for the lead; true closers face the greatest risk if the pace proves moderate. The field holds more prominent-minded horses than the race can accommodate up front, with Mallavelly best placed to secure the lead, and Sanctijude — the most straightforward pressing type among the remainder — most likely to settle into a genuine second or third position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mallavelly Dictates, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Mallavelly establishes a clear, uncontested lead and sets a sustainable pace that denies closers enough time to get competitive.
scenarios.body: Mallavelly, guided by Colin Keane, idles along on the front end at her own tempo on Good to Firm ground and simply never comes off the bridle long enough for the hold-up fillies to reel her in; a small field of six means there is no real weight of pace to sustain the race shape late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Presser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mallavelly's early fractions are just honest enough that a close-tracking filly can collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Sanctijude, racing prominently in behind, is the natural beneficiary if Mallavelly ties up slightly on the flat Curragh straight; her winning form at 8f on Good ground and Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard makes her the most credible challenger from this position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mallavelly goes too fast too soon and the pace collapses entering the final two furlongs, gifting time to the deep hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Orchidaceae has the strongest profile in similar going conditions (8/9 in good-ground handicaps) and W J Lee knows how to produce her late, but she needs a truly run race to generate momentum from the rear in a small field — the risk is that Mallavelly is never pressured and the pace is too modest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Kirkland Sioux or Glitter And Glory manage to force their way forward early and create a multi-horse battle for the lead that burns Mallavelly off.
scenarios.body: Both are redistributed types racing against their natural role in this shape and carry meaningful style-fit discounts, so a scenario that depends on them dominating is inherently low-probability; however, if Glitter And Glory uses her fresh legs (only 6 days since last run) to press aggressively, the race order could be scrambled.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Kirkland Sioux or Glitter And Glory challenge Mallavelly for the early lead — if either forces a pace battle in the first two furlongs, it could transform this from a solo-dictation race into one that genuinely suits late closers like Orchidaceae.
Glitter And Glory runs only six days after her last outing; monitor her in the parade ring for any signs of post-race fatigue before factoring her into the finish picture.

Pink Oxalis is 37 days fresh and switches back to a turf handicap — her blinkered run on Good ground needs to be sharp from the break if she is to avoid being stranded at the rear in a slowly-run six-runner field.

Sanctijude is a 3-year-old carrying 124lbs against older fillies — if Dylan Browne McMonagle can slot her into an uncontested second or third behind Mallavelly, the weight advantage combined with her recent winning form over the trip makes her the primary tactical threat to the leader.

The Good to Firm going report (confirmed across multiple races at the Curragh today) is the best surface profile for Orchidaceae, who has strong form figures in identical conditions — monitor market moves if punters believe the pace will be strong enough to bring her late run into play.

races.name: 1xBet.ie Proud Supporters Of Irish Racing Curragh Cup (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Al Riffa
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter who should enjoy a clear lead on Good to Firm ground, but recent form figures (74-634) are modest for a Group 2 and his style-fit tag at this distance and in this role should temper expectations; 31 days since his last run and dropping back slightly in class.

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer who needs a genuinely strong gallop to close from the rear; Rossa Ryan takes over for a trainer who has had a quiet 14-day record (0 from 12), and similar-going form of 10/15 with no wins is a concern at this level.

runners_data.name: Green Impact
runners_data.note: John Harrington's four-year-old has strong similar-going form (8/9) and has won at this trip, but the redistribution reflects the crowded prominent division — she is a natural racer close to the pace and will need to fight to secure that berth over 1m6f against stronger rivals; 56-day absence is notable.

runners_data.name: Happy Pharoah
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien saddles this four-year-old who has solid similar-going form but a poor recent sequence including a 26th place finish; a natural front-runner whose redistribution to midfield reflects the pace congestion, and 65 days off the track adds an element of uncertainty about readiness.

runners_data.name: Illinois
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount on a five-year-old who has Group-level form at this sort of trip, winning over 22f on Good and placing at 16f; travelled well close to pace in recent runs and his natural style fits this race shape ideally without any redistribution flag — the key contender.

runners_data.name: Tennessee Stud
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's four-year-old is a natural front-runner pushed back by pace congestion — he will likely attempt to push forward regardless, and his victory over 15f on Heavy ground shows stamina; however, the form figures (441-03) include a disappointing third last time, and 51 days off compounds the query.

runners_data.name: Trustyourinstinct
runners_data.note: O'Brien's six-year-old comes here on the back of a win (form 6-7212 with four wins from fifteen on similar going) and was only 21 days ago — fresh and in form; a prominent racer who fits naturally just off the pace without redistribution and has course-relevant experience, making him a well-placed participant.

runners_data.name: Floresta
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's filly ran just 11 days ago and has a strong similar-going record (6/8) with two wins at 14f on Good; a natural front-runner who will press for a prominent position even if the map shows her in midfield, and the p-headgear entry signals she wears a hood — her last-start win (215-01) is an encouraging trend.

races.paceDynamic: Al Riffa is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead, he should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m6f trip on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a measured fractions race favours those who can travel close to the pace and quicken off a sound but undemanding tempo. Illinois and Trustyourinstinct are the horses best positioned to track Al Riffa without racing out of role, putting them in an advantageous tactical spot. Horses who close into a true pace should thrive here, as should those who can sit just off the leader and pounce entering the straight; hold-up horses face a stiffer ask if the gallop is modest. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all find their natural position — Tennessee Stud, Green Impact, Floresta and Happy Pharoah are all genuine prominent racers but are redistributed to midfield in this map; of these, Tennessee Stud and Floresta, with their pattern of positive racing, are most likely to push forward and compete for a handy berth, though they cannot all get it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Al Riffa Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Al Riffa sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race only truly ignites in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Al Riffa's controlled gallop compresses the field and creates a bunched, tactical finish where horses who have travelled smoothly just off the pace — Illinois and Trustyourinstinct — are ideally placed to quicken; the Good to Firm ground rewards horses with a clean stride and those who haven't had to fight for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up, Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If several redistributed horses push forward and create a genuinely contested early pace that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: With Tennessee Stud and Floresta competing for prominent positions, the tempo becomes more genuine, suiting horses who handle strong pace and have the class to sustain it through the final stages on fast ground; Illinois, proven at the trip and course type, and Floresta — a genuine front-runner getting back to her best — both benefit from a proper test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough to set up a strong late run from the back of the field.
scenarios.body: Dallas Star would need the tempo to be strong throughout to peg back prominent leaders from her hold-up position, while Happy Pharoah, a natural prominent type running from midfield, would need an unusually strong fractions race to finish from off the pace; this scenario is less likely given the lone front-runner dynamic and the risk that moderate pace strands true hold-up types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Al Riffa gets a soft lead, dictates a crawl and simply outstays rivals who cannot quicken on the fast ground.
scenarios.body: Al Riffa stealing the race on his own terms is a live but low-probability outcome — he is clearly capable over this trip but his recent form is modest and rivals like Illinois and Trustyourinstinct should be travelling powerfully enough to reel him in off a true lead; the style-fit flag on Al Riffa also tempers confidence in this outcome.

watchPoints.text: Illinois (Ryan Moore) is the horse to watch most closely — if he travels smoothly just off Al Riffa's pace through the first mile, he is ideally positioned to devastate a steady-run race with a sustained run from the two-furlong pole.

The redistribution of Tennessee Stud, Floresta and Happy Pharoah all competing for prominent positions could create an unexpectedly contested pace — if multiple horses push forward from their mapped positions, the tempo could lift sharply and unsettle the race shape entirely.

Floresta's 11-day turnaround and hood (headgear: p) are both factors to monitor in the pre-race — if she is keen or unruly, she could disrupt Al Riffa's rhythm and manufacture a stronger gallop than the lone-leader scenario implies.

Dallas Star's hold-up profile makes her entirely dependent on pace; if Al Riffa trots in front as expected on this fast ground, watch for her failing to land a blow and finishing well but too late — a strong drifter if the gallop proves modest.

Trustyourinstinct's 21-day turnaround after a win is worth monitoring — O'Brien runners returning quickly in good form often run well, and if he settles kindly behind Al Riffa in second or third, he could prove a durable threat at the business end.

races.name: James Nolan Bar Kildare Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, winning over 5f at Heathrow on good-to-firm before two efforts on good ground at the Curragh; goes up in trip to 6f but has the pace to dictate here, though 52 days off and a style-fit flag at 0.93 mean he is not a gilt-edged proposition — he is simply the horse most likely to get to the front.

runners_data.name: Tradewinds
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form (3-2-3-2) and the only genuine prominent runner other than Lars Soldier; fitted with headgear, trained by Donnacha O'Brien and freshened up on 16 days since a 6f effort on good ground — the most natural second horse in the race shape and best placed to capitalise if the leader tires.

runners_data.name: Desert Alchemist
runners_data.note: Improved when stepped up to 6f last time out (3rd at the Curragh on soft), and Good to Firm is a slight question mark given his soft-ground placing; Luke McAteer takes over and David Marnane's yard has placed 2 from 20 runners over the last fortnight, suggesting a quiet stable spell, but 6f on quicker ground is the right profile.

runners_data.name: I Ready
runners_data.note: Three consecutive finishes of 8th, 5th and 6th all on good ground at 6f, with Colin Keane in the saddle suggesting connections expect a better showing; however, the consistent mid-pack finishes and a headgear flag point to a horse who is finding his level rather than threatening a win, and his hold-up style means he needs pace to run into.

runners_data.name: Seven Nation Army
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for Joseph O'Brien but the horse has posted three poor efforts (6-8-8) and fades in the finish — his natural hold-up style has placed him mid-map by necessity, as the rear is over-subscribed, which means he is unlikely to be running from his most comfortable base position.

runners_data.name: Belle Island
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 5f on standard ground (3rd and 2nd) but has failed to hit the frame since stepping up to 6f or onto more testing surfaces; Robson De Aguiar's yard has gone 0 from 12 in the last fortnight, and while she's a natural hold-up horse, being shuffled forward from her ideal position does her no favours in a race with one clear pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Lucy's Promise
runners_data.note: Three Curragh outings all at 6f on good ground have yielded finishes of 12th, 7th and 6th — a hold-up horse with no win or placing to her name and no obvious reason to upgrade on those efforts; Shane Foley rides but the form string offers little encouragement, and the race shape does not set up for deep closers.

runners_data.name: Woodlawn Lily
runners_data.note: John Murtagh's filly has run three times, all at 5f, so this step up to 6f is an unknown; her best effort was a 4th on soft ground, and the Good to Firm conditions today add further uncertainty — a genuine hold-up type by style, she is being mapped closer to proceedings than her natural racing pattern would suggest.

races.paceDynamic: Lars Soldier is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner 6f nursery handicap on Good to Firm at the Curragh, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, he can dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the gates. Tradewinds is the only genuine prominent type, likely to settle just behind Lars Soldier in second or third, while the remainder of the field — Seven Nation Army, Belle Island, Lucy's Promise and Woodlawn Lily — are all natural hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is no room for them all at the rear; the true back of the field will be thinly populated. This race shape — a lone pace-setter controlling fractions on fast ground over a straight 6f — strongly favours horses who can race close to the tempo and quicken in the straight, rather than deep closers who will need a genuine collapse in the leader to get involved. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can genuinely accommodate at the rear, and Lars Soldier and Tradewinds are the most likely horses to actually secure their natural positions; prominent and pace-pressing profiles hold the structural advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lars Soldier Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lars Soldier gets a clean break and settles into a comfortable lead at a sustainable pace on the fast ground, dictating throughout.
scenarios.body: He travels widest and fastest in his own time, using the Good to Firm conditions to maintain a strong but measured gallop that burns off hold-up types in the straight; no rival has the early foot to challenge him for the lead. Tradewinds, sitting close in his slipstream, is the most likely beneficiary if Lars Soldier ties up late, but the map strongly favours the front-running profile here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Presser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lars Soldier sets a fraction quick enough to tire in the final furlong, inviting Tradewinds or a pace-pressing type to wear him down.
scenarios.body: Tradewinds, travelling prominently throughout, is ideally placed to absorb the pace and pick up as Lars Soldier's effort flattens out in the closing stages; this scenario suits a horse who can race within themselves before delivering a strong, sustained finish. Desert Alchemist, stepping up to 6f on a suitable surface, could also make a late charge from midfield if the pace is genuinely strong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to leave the field strung out and create a true end-to-end gallop that catches the hold-up types late.
scenarios.body: Seven Nation Army or Belle Island, though pushed forward from their natural rear position, could still mount a late run if they find clearer ground in the straight and the pace genuinely collapses; however, their REDISTRIBUTED status and modest recent form in similar conditions reduces the likelihood of this materialising. This scenario is structurally undermined by the fact that the true hold-up horses have been crowded into midfield and are not running from their optimal base.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Lands Gamble
scenarios.trigger: If a significantly improved performance from a lightly-raced or freshened runner overturns the pace map entirely.
scenarios.body: Woodlawn Lily, stepping up to 6f for John Murtagh with a market move, or Lucy's Promise catching the field flat-footed, could spring a surprise if their handicap mark is ahead of what their recent form suggests; these are low-probability outcomes dependent on hidden improvement rather than tactical advantage. The pace shape does not set this up, making it a marginal punt scenario only.

watchPoints.text: Lars Soldier — monitor the early stalls break; if he misses the break or is taken on for the lead unexpectedly, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the prominent/pressing horses gain a major advantage.

Tradewinds — watch market moves at the off; consistent placed form, a yard in decent recent form (4/14 in 14 days), headgear applied, and a jockey booking that looks purposeful suggest he could be sent off shorter than his OR of 82 implies.

Seven Nation Army — Dylan Browne McMonagle is a top booking for a horse with very modest recent form; if there is stable confidence here it would represent a significant turnaround, though the fading-in-finish tag and redistribution from rear to midfield are material concerns.

Desert Alchemist — the only runner with a form line showing improvement stepping up to 6f, and his 3rd on soft at the Curragh last time is the most relevant piece of recent form in the field; watch whether he is allowed to coast into the race from midfield rather than chase the pace.

Woodlawn Lily — untested at 6f and Good to Firm, this is a speculative step-up in trip for Murtagh; her price in the market may reflect stable expectation of improvement and is worth monitoring before the off.

races.name: Final Furlong Podcast With 1xBet.ie Irish EBF Maiden
